questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Cannot go over the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot go over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete your pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to wait until you start the engine before getting on. They should sit forward, not crowding you, and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam both day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.
0.3 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, riders age 21 or older cannot ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Riding may be unsafe even at lower levels.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Less experienced riders should lead the group.
Less experienced riders should be near the front.
Less experienced riders should be at the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less experienced riders should be near the front.
questions.explanation: Put less experienced riders near the front behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the newer riders at the same time.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay within the posted speed limit.
Go over the speed limit by no more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within legal speed limits. Pass only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may give poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, you should be in:

options.text: A single-file line.
Pairs.
A staggered line.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file line.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered line. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect from wind, but a windshield doesn't.
A windshield protects from wind, but goggles don't.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect from wind, but a windshield doesn't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How should you swerve to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. Use a small amount of pressure.

questions.question: What is true about operating a motorized scooter?

options.text: You can only ride during the day.
You do not need a driver license.
You can ride with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can ride with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, you can operate a motorized scooter if you have any class of driver license.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to avoid hazards like opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: What should you do when making a U-turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Use the rear brake instead to control your speed.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Wherever you feel most comfortable.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: The left portion of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid opening doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Be ready to change position if traffic or road conditions change.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: In the left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
In the right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It can change based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position at all times. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Change your position as traffic and road conditions change.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how fast it is consumed. How often a person drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When wearing a protective jacket in hot weather, what should you do?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on for protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on for protection.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy riding jacket to protect you from injury in a crash. Jackets also protect you from dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to prevent overheating.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when the bike turns or curves.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when the bike turns or curves.
questions.explanation: Before your passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction you will turn or curve. This helps you and the bike lean the right way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation teaches the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hand over the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when entering an intersection. Keep your hand ready over the clutch and both brakes so you can respond quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a full stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: How should you brake during a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: Is it good to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you will never get used to any part of the lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, when you need to adjust to changing conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, when you need to adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle like a motorcycle is going or where it is. Do not assume other drivers can accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's brake light is usually not as bright as a larger vehicle's, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not notice when you brake.

questions.question: When should you shift gears while turning?

options.text: Only if you can shift smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the curve.
It is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you can shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you turn. If you must shift while turning, shift smoothly. A sudden change in power can cause your rear wheel to slide.
